rule: Every library and asset in Tap Party comes from a repo that 2three1y has starred on GitHub. tools/check-starred.mjs checks this list against starred.txt.

credits.name: trystero
credits.author: Dan Motzenbecker
credits.used_for: Rooms with no server. Browsers find each other through public Nostr relays, then send taps and messages straight to each other over WebRTC.
credits.changes: None to the code. Source map comments were removed because the maps are not included.

credits.name: morse-learn
credits.author: Google Inc. (made by Tania Finlayson and Use All Five with Google Creative Lab)
credits.used_for: Learn mode: the Morse letter table, the order letters are taught in (E, T, A, I, M, S…), the rule that a letter counts as learned after 2 right answers, and the practice word list.
credits.changes: Pieces of scripts/morse-dictionary.js, scripts/words.js, scripts/game-state.js and scripts/config.js were combined into one ES module. The reverse lookup table is now built from englishToMorse, because the original had a typo for the letter V. The file says so at the top.
credits.notice: Copyright 2018 Google Inc. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. This is not an officially supported Google product. The morse-learn repo has no NOTICE file; its copyright notice and licence are kept in the file and in licenses/morse-learn.txt.

credits.name: web-haptics
credits.author: Lochie Axon
credits.used_for: Haptics. On Android it uses navigator.vibrate. On iPhone, which has no navigator.vibrate, it clicks a hidden iOS switch control so the Taptic Engine ticks.

credits.name: braille
credits.author: Nonemoticoner
credits.used_for: Braille view: turns decoded text into Unicode braille cells.
credits.changes: module.exports was changed to an ES module export. app/braille-text.js adds the number sign and the Unified English Braille punctuation cells before calling it.

credits.name: tabbable
credits.author: David Clark and the focus-trap contributors
credits.used_for: Finds the buttons and fields inside a dialog, so Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside it.
credits.changes: None to the code. The source map comment was removed.

credits.name: a11y-dialog
credits.author: Kitty Giraudel
credits.used_for: The Settings dialog and the Leave room dialog: focus moves in and back out, Escape closes, and the rest of the page is hidden from screen readers while it is open.
credits.changes: The published build bundles a package called focusable-selectors, which is not starred. That part was removed and the focus trap now uses tabbable instead. The file says so at the top.

credits.name: dart-bip340
credits.author: fiatjaf
credits.used_for: Nostr relays only accept signed events. trystero normally signs them with @noble/secp256k1, which is not starred, so Tap Party signs with a JavaScript port of this repo's BIP-340 Schnorr code instead.
credits.changes: Ported from Dart to JavaScript. The curve maths that the Dart code takes from pointycastle is written from scratch. It passes the official BIP-340 signing test vectors.

not_used.why: Its sound packs come from many people and none of them states its own licence, so they are not safe to reuse. Every tone and earcon in Tap Party is made with WebAudio oscillators instead, with no sound files at all.
trystero's Nostr strategy depends on it, but it is not starred, so it is replaced by the dart-bip340 port above.
Bundled inside a11y-dialog's published build, but not starred, so it was swapped for tabbable.

testing_only.why: Ran an automated accessibility check during testing. It is not part of the site.
